claims.text: The driver's own trace never places him inside the pickup geofence. EV-GPS-00206 is impaired (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8, median 18 s against a nominal 10 s cadence) and I disclose that, but the impairment does not touch the distance measurement: across all 52 driver fixes the closest he ever came to the pin was 284.95 m, his mean distance was 1,704.82 m and his maximum 5,480.89 m. The arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup is 120 m. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limb (b) fails on the driver's own telemetry, which is enough on its own to make the $4.00 cancellation fee unchargeable.

Limb (c) fails independently of limb (b). The derived arrival analysis records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds against the 300 second minimum dwell for LARGE_VENUE - a 300 second shortfall, not a marginal one - because a driver who never entered the 120 m radius cannot have held position inside it. The minimum dwell is the consideration the fee is meant to buy, and none of it was delivered to this rider. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

Limb (d) also fails, and it fails on the trip record alone, which carries full weight. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. POL-NS-01 says in terms that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE 'is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and does not satisfy limb (d)', and directs such a trip to POL-NS-03. On a conjunctive test, that single failure disposes of the charge.

Under POL-NS-02 the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. That clause refunds in full where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation; here 0 of 52 driver fixes qualified, the trace spans 15:03:30 to the 15:18:40 cancellation, and the derived analysis confirms qualifying_fix_count 0. The driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the $4.00 comes back. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

Even if the Judge takes the wrong-entrance route, the fee still comes back in full. POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03 where the driver was stationary for the required dwell outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin, and 284.95 m sits inside that ceiling. POL-NS-03 then states its own outcome: the driver 'did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full'. Whichever route is taken, the rider's SGD 4.00 is returned; the only question POL-NS-03 leaves open is who absorbs the driver's cost, and that is answered against the platform, not the rider. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

The fault allocation under POL-NS-03 confirms the rider should not fund anything. The chat log holds only two SYSTEM notifications, with no sub-location named by either party, and the trip record shows 4 registered pickup points for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. POL-NS-03(ii) therefore applies: the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver's 50 per cent goodwill payment is charged to the platform and 'never recovered from the rider'. The rider's refund is a clean SGD 4.00 with no set-off against it.

The rider's conduct is not in issue. Her own track places her device within 22.50 m of the pin at its furthest and 15.43 m on average, with all 31 rider fixes qualifying under the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius - she was standing at the pin the app gave her. I do not run POL-NS-04's exoneration route: the chat log contains only system messages, so limb (a) cannot be made out and I do not ask the Judge to treat that clause as engaged. But the presence threshold it sets is comfortably satisfied, and the failure in this trip lies entirely on the driver's side of the transaction. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road, and that closes the only door the driver has to a longer clock. EV-ADVIS-00206-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory carrying KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed at all. The limb is unavailable, and in any event there is nothing to sum: the derived runs list is empty with run_count 0 and accumulated_sec 0.0. The driver cannot be carried past the 300 second minimum through that door. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

The trace's schema-level impairment is not a policy-level impairment and should not push this case to a reviewer. No limb of POL-NS-08 bites: the largest sampling interval is 26 s against the 120 s gap threshold and the gaps list is empty; the trace holds 52 fixes against the 6-fix minimum and 31 rider fixes; the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2 with contiguous msg_ids; and the 4.00 cancellation fee reconciles with the LARGE_VENUE zone fee and the RYDE_X tier fee, so there is no fare defect. POL-GEN-02's confidence cap is therefore not dragged below the 0.70 floor, and in any event the deciding fact is carried on two independent artifacts - the GPS trace at 0.8 and the trip record at 1.0 - so the cap is the maximum, 1.0. No limb of POL-NS-09 is engaged and the case is decidable on the papers.

The amount to be returned is exactly SGD 4.00. The payments ledger shows one line only - cancellation_fee 4.00, with base_fare, distance_fare, time_fare, waiting_time_fee and platform_fee all 0.00 - charged at 15:18:57 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-NS-06 directs a refund of the cancellation-fee line and not of any booking or platform fee; here there is nothing else on the ledger to carve out, so the whole of the contested amount is returned.

Escalation on profile grounds is not available to the driver either. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d counters read 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and POL-NS-09(d) are not engaged, and there is no pattern of repeat no-show disputes between these two parties. The driver's own numbers - no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 187 - do not trip the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check, because 1 is below the count of 4 and 1/187 is far below the rate of 0.08. Nothing here displaces a ruling on the merits, and the fee is already charged, so a hold would leave the rider out of pocket for a review the record does not need.

POL-NS-07's 80 per cent driver compensation is not available on this record. That clause operates only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full', which cannot be said where limb (b) and limb (d) both fail. The driver's only route to money, if any, is the platform-funded half-fee goodwill in POL-NS-03(ii), which cannot be charged back to the rider. The rider should not be paying a $3.20 driver compensation out of a $4.00 fee for a pickup the driver never reached, and the fare ledger should show nothing taken from her.

The driver does not contest the substance of the rider's account. His filed statement concedes that the map put him at 'the HarbourFront kerb' while the pin was the VivoCity Lobby L ride-hailing pickup, and that he does not blame the passenger. That admission matches the trace's closest approach of 284.95 m to the pin and leaves the cancellation fee with no basis in this trip's own evidence. (EV-GPS-00206 impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8 - disclosed.)

claims.text: The trip record fixes this pickup as LARGE_VENUE with 4 registered pickup points at VivoCity. That is the fact POL-NS-03(ii) turns on: where neither party named a sub-location and the venue has 2 or more registered pickup points, the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party.

The chat log contains two SYSTEM notifications and nothing else. Neither party named a sub-location in it; the admissibility note says that silence is what carries POL-NS-03(ii). The first message, 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.', is sent by SYSTEM, not by the rider, so it is not a rider statement of a sub-location for POL-NS-03(i).

The GPS trace is IMPAIRED: issue code LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight_multiplier 0.8. I disclose that impairment. Its derived driver_track.min_distance_m is 284.95 m from the pickup pin, outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, and the pre-pass records the stationary position 285 m from the pin as established beyond argument. POL-NS-02's arrival test yields to POL-NS-03 on exactly these facts, so the wrong-entrance clause governs.

The driver held position for the required 300 s for LARGE_VENUE: the trip record's wait_time_min is 6.6 min (396 s) and the arrived event at 15:12:05 to cancellation at 15:18:40 is 395 s. The GPS pre-pass records 22 fixes spanning the 400 s dwell, so the POL-NS-03 stationary-dwell requirement is met despite the trace's LOW_SAMPLE_RATE impairment (weight 0.8, disclosed).

POL-NS-05 does not make this a false arrival. The arrival marker at 15:12:05 was placed while the driver was stationary 284.95 m from the pin, under the 300 m false-marker threshold and not at 15 km/h or above, and POL-NS-05 expressly routes a stationary driver within 300 m but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03. The trace's LOW_SAMPLE_RATE impairment (weight 0.8) is disclosed.

The cancellation reason code is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. POL-NS-01 limb (d) therefore fails and the fee cannot be charged under POL-NS-01; the case is governed by POL-NS-03, which is the clause that carries the driver's goodwill payment.

The anti-farming check does not trip and cannot be used to withhold payment. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb of POL-NS-07, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d (187) is 0.0053, below the 0.08 rate limb. The driver profile therefore does not support withholding.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger applies. POL-NS-08(b) trace defect is not met because gaps is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and there are 52 fixes; the schema-level LOW_SAMPLE_RATE tag at weight 0.8 is above the 0.70 escalation floor and does not make the trace undecidable. The case should be decided on the merits, not escalated.

The goodwill amount under POL-NS-03(ii) is 50% of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in the fare breakdown, i.e. SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. That is the driver-side remedy this record supports.

ruling.explanation:
What happened, on the record. The app pinned the pickup at the VivoCity Level 1 Lobby L ride-hailing bay; the driver's map placed him at the HarbourFront Centre kerb, about 285 m away. He waited roughly six and a half minutes and then cancelled, selecting the reason 'driver unable to locate'. Neither party named a sub-location in the in-app chat, and VivoCity carries four registered pickup points on the trip record. The rider's own track puts her within about 23 m of the pin throughout the wait.

The $4.00 cancellation fee does not stand. POL-NS-01 permits the fee only if all four of its conditions hold. Condition (b) fails: the driver's own GPS trace never brings him inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius - his closest approach over the whole trip was 284.95 m. Condition (d) fails too: the trip was terminated with reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes the clause accepts. One failure would be enough; both fail.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee is the only amount charged, so the whole of the contested amount is returned.

Who absorbs the driver's cost. Under POL-NS-03(ii), because neither party specified a sub-location and this venue has two or more registered pickup points (four), the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party. The driver therefore receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50% of the fee - SGD 2.00 - charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. Neither of you is blamed for a mapping failure; the two figures are independent and are not netted against each other.

Arguments considered. (1) The driver's POL-NS-03 case is accepted: he held position for well over the 300 s minimum within 400 m of the pin, so POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03 and the registered-pickup-point count supports the pin-ambiguity allocation. (2) POL-NS-05 false-arrival marker, and any false-arrival referral, is not engaged: when the driver tapped 'arrived' he was stationary within 300 m of the pin, which POL-NS-05 expressly routes to POL-NS-03 rather than treating as a false marker. (3) POL-NS-06(i) dwell summing is unavailable: EV-ADVIS-00206-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so the limb cannot be run, and there were no separate in-geofence intervals to sum in any event - no advisory lengthens the clock. (4) POL-NS-07's 80% driver compensation is unavailable because it operates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; separately, the anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination against 187 completed trips). (5) POL-NS-04 rider-contact exoneration is not engaged, because the chat holds only two system notifications and limb (a) needs a locating message from the rider; the rider's presence is nonetheless not in issue. (6) Escalation is not warranted: the GPS trace's only defect is a schema-level LOW_SAMPLE_RATE (weight 0.8), and under POL-NS-08's own limbs nothing bites (largest sampling interval 26 s against the 120 s threshold, 52 fixes, chat count and fare line reconcile), so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, no POL-NS-09(e) escalation arises, and there is no direct contradiction, repeat-dispute pattern or abuse counter. Confidence of 0.80 is above the 0.70 floor.

Evidence and weight. The deciding fact - that the driver never reached the pickup pin - is carried by the positional GPS trace EV-GPS-00206, which is impaired at weight 0.8 with issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE. That impairment is named and the finding survives it: the distance measurement does not depend on sampling cadence. The driver's filed statement is an admission against his own interest (the map put him at the wrong kerb, and he does not blame the passenger) and it agrees with the trace; as a counterparty statement it carries no weight multiplier and so does not move the confidence cap, which is set at 0.80 by the trace. Two rider claims were discarded at the citation check for citing the impaired trace without naming its issue code; they are listed in the audit record below.
